arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Michael McConnell argued for Delaware. He cited federalism principles. He said states set official qualifications.
Chief Justice Roberts asked about standing. He noted Adams is ready to apply. He questioned if Adams is truly interested.
Justice Thomas asked about elected judges. He wondered if the argument changes for elected positions.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Delaware law requires judges to live in the state. Adams wants to run for office. The state says residency is a valid qualification.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 4, lines 22-18

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on October 5, 2020.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 4, lines 10-20

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Adams wants to run for judge despite living out of state.
Delaware wants to keep its residency requirement for judges.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 4, lines 22-18

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Adams argues the residency rule violates equal protection principles.
Delaware argues states control qualifications for high-ranking officials.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 4, lines 22-18

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Does Adams have standing to sue if he is ready to apply?
Does the residency rule change if judges are elected instead of appointed?
